day_summary: Juneteenth — US equity markets closed. No SPCX trading. SPCX is in STEP_ASIDE mode following the June 18 stop trigger at $174.90 (−8.82% on Day 5 post-IPO). The $185 daily close stop defined in the entry framework was triggered $10.10 below the threshold — the framework is unambiguous: exit position, do not re-enter until two consecutive daily closes above $185 on above-average volume. The Juneteenth holiday creates a 3-day gap (June 19–21) with no equity trading before the June 22 (Monday) reassessment session. Key context during the holiday: (1) No new SPCX price data — last official close $174.90 (June 18); (2) Macro: DXY at 100.75 on Juneteenth FX trading (worsening from 100.15) — the highest-multiple name in the US market (84x 2025 revenue) remains most exposed to rate-discount compression; (3) June 20 weekly options expiry resolves tomorrow — the $195 max-pain structure expires (well above $174.90), clearing the gamma headwind; (4) UFO ETF passive bid still in the 2–4 week window post-IPO (Day 5 to today), but decelerating as the MSCI rebalancing approaches completion. The reassessment window opens June 22: if SPCX opens at $165–$175 on June 22 with recovering volume (above 150M shares), the 3–5 session stabilization watch begins.

outlook.short_term: Step aside — reassessment pending June 22. The $185 stop was triggered at $174.90; the framework requires exit. June 22 is the first diagnostic: (1) SPCX opens $165–$175 with recovering volume → begin 3–5 session stabilization watch; new stop $165, July put hedge; (2) SPCX opens below $165 → correction extending, next test $150–$160, no action until $150 holds on two sessions; (3) SPCX opens above $185 on gap-up (unlikely given macro) → two-day recovery confirmation needed before re-entry. The June 20 weekly expiry (tomorrow) clears the $195 gamma headwind, giving June 22 a cleaner technical slate. Do not catch the falling knife — disciplined stabilization watching is the playbook.
outlook.long_term: Generational franchise unchanged. Starlink 5M+ subs growing ~40% annually, Starship, Starshield, Cursor AI ($60B), and the June 12 largest-ever IPO at $135 ($75B raise) define a unique infrastructure-technology franchise. At $174.90 and ~84x 2025 revenue, the valuation is still extreme but compressed from the Day 3 peak of ~94x. September 2 first earnings print is the fundamental anchor: Starlink subscriber count, Starship launch cadence, Cursor AI revenue, and Starshield contract disclosures will either validate or reset the $2.4T market cap. December 9 lock-up expiry is the first major float expansion event. Patient capital at $165–$175 (properly hedged with July puts) is a better structural entry than $190–$200 at IPO launch.

bull_case: June 20 weekly options expiry tomorrow — the $195 max-pain gamma headwind that created mechanical selling pressure below $195 expires at 4 PM ET; June 22 session starts with a clean options slate; this removes one of the three structural headwinds that drove the Day 5 selloff (alongside FOMC hawkish repricing and MSCI bid deceleration).

bear_case: $185 stop triggered at $174.90 — the framework's own risk management exited the position; a stop trigger after a failed entry ($190–$200 zone) is the clearest technical signal that the near-term thesis is wrong; the next test is whether $165 holds or the correction extends to $150–$160 before the first earnings anchor (September 2).

DXY at 100.75 on Juneteenth FX trading — the highest-multiple name in the US market (84x revenue, net losses) remains most exposed to Warsh's hawkish dots; if DXY holds above 100 through June 22, the FOMC discount-rate compression on SPCX's multiple continues; a single Warsh hawkish speech between June 22–26 could re-accelerate the selloff.

MSCI passive bid decelerating — Day 6 post-IPO brings the structural forced-buyer closer to exhaustion; if June 22 volume falls below 100M shares, the passive bid has run its course and the next marginal buyer is retail, not institutional; retail-driven floors are weaker than institutional-driven floors.

First post-IPO earnings September 2 — SPCX must disclose the actual Starlink subscriber count, Starship cadence, and Cursor AI contribution against a $2.4T market cap (84x revenue); if any metric disappoints versus the implied expectations, the correction from $174.90 has further room to go; the June–August period before earnings is the highest-uncertainty window.
